        *   Deletes the shadowed file and returns the resource object that was deleted.
    *   Expose 'schema', 'validate', 'create', 'update', 'read', 'destroy', and 'plan' exports in the shadow-file module.

*   Ensure the file resource's create operation:

The `shadow-file.js` provider lives at `packages/gatsby/src/recipes/providers/gatsby/shadow-file.js` and was introduced as part of the initial Gatsby Recipes release. It was added via "feat(recipes): Implement shadow file resource and test it (#23063)," which also included a call to ensureFile.

### What Recipes Are

Recipes is an "infrastructure as code" system that lets users automatically manage and provision the technology stack for their Gatsby site/app through code rather than manual processes. It's powered by React & MDX and a useful analogy is "React Native for Infrastructure."

Recipes also provides a read/write API for Desktop/Admin to build lowcode tooling on top of Gatsby & integrated services. It's designed to be extensible so new capabilities can be added which allow Recipes to automate more things.

### The GatsbyShadowFile Component

The shadow-file provider powers the `<GatsbyShadowFile>` recipe component. Its API takes two props: theme: the name of the theme (or plugin) which provides the file you'd like to shadow, and path: the path to the file within the theme. E.g. the example file above lives at node_modules/gatsby-theme-blog/src/components/seo.js.

A usage example is `<GatsbyShadowFile theme="gatsby-theme-blog" path="src/components/seo.js" />`.

### Provider Architecture (create/read/destroy/plan)

Gatsby Recipes providers follow a resource model with functions like `create`, `read`, `destroy`, and `plan`. Note that the provider structure evolved over time — a later change "moves gatsby plugin provider to new structure for resources."

A key design principle was safety: all recipes should never overwrite a user's code or configuration. The recipes should check if the thing they are writing/removing are possible without destructive changes and ask for confirmation/fail if they are not.

### Background on Shadowing (what the provider automates)

The shadow-file provider automates Gatsby's shadowing feature. Gatsby themes introduce a concept called "shadowing." This feature allows users to replace a file in the src directory that is included in the webpack bundle with their own implementation. In order to override a component in a theme, you create a correspondingly-named file — any file that lives in the src/gatsby-theme-blog directory of the user's site will be used instead of a file with the same name located in the theme's src directory.
